title: Lightning Hit the Empire State Building 8 Times in 24 Minutes

scenes.text: Lightning hit the Empire State Building eight times in 24 minutes.
It gets struck about 25 times every year.
That's because it's one of the tallest things around. Lightning takes the easiest path to the ground.
A metal rod on top catches each bolt, and thick wires carry it safely down.
A bolt is around five times hotter than the surface of the Sun. The building just shrugs it off.
Eight strikes. Twenty-four minutes. Still standing.

description:
Lightning hit the Empire State Building eight times in 24 minutes.
The skyscraper is struck about 25 times a year, and a rod on top gives each bolt a safe path to the ground.
Would you watch a storm from inside it?
first_comment: The rod doesn't attract lightning, it only gives it a safe path down. Would you go up the building in a thunderstorm?
